signals.text: The owner wants the longest line, measured in words, added to the wordcount output.
signals.possible_indication: The owner needs a line-length view that words, characters and lines do not give.

signals.text: The output today reports `words: N characters: N lines: N` and has no longest-line figure.
The new field reports a single number. It has no line number and no line text.
signals.possible_indication: The owner wants a compact figure, not a diagnostic report.

signals.text: The unterminated final segment counts as a line for the longest-line measure, so `a b c` with no terminator reports 3.
signals.possible_indication: The longest-line measure and the existing `lines` field treat the same final segment differently.

signals.text: The existing `lines` counter does not count an unterminated final segment, so `a b c` reports `lines: 0`.
signals.possible_indication: Readers may see `lines: 0` next to `longest_line_words: 3` and think the output contradicts itself.

signals.text: The change must reuse the word definition and the line terminator set from SPEC-0001 to SPEC-0005.
signals.possible_indication: The owner wants one meaning of word and line across all fields.

signals.text: The change adds no third-party runtime dependency.
The new field uses the label `longest_line_words: N` and comes last, so the line reads `words: W characters: C lines: L longest_line_words: N`.
The existing fields and their meaning must stay stable for both `wordcount PATH` and `wordcount -`.
signals.possible_indication: Existing users and scripts parse the current output.

signals.text: The README and the existing tests assert the three-field output line, so they no longer match the new output.
signals.possible_indication: The README, the tests and the specs need updates, and the Quality Gate must still pass.

DISCOVER.core_issue: The wordcount output does not report how many words the longest line holds, so users cannot see line length in words.
DISCOVER.impact_value: Users get a longest-line figure without extra tools. The value is convenience only, with no failure to fix. Existing parsers must keep working.
DISCOVER.discovery_method: Owner feature intent, the existing SPEC-0001 to SPEC-0005, and the human answers to three clarification questions.
DISCOVER.pattern_dependencies: The missing longest-line metric is the root pattern. The final-segment rule, the definition reuse and the output contract all constrain how that metric behaves. The final-segment rule differs from the existing `lines` rule, so the documentation must explain the difference. The new field changes the output line, so the README and the tests that assert the three-field line become stale.

pattern_narratives.applies_to: The wordcount CLI output for files and standard input.
pattern_narratives.severity: Low. This is an enhancement, not a defect.
pattern_narratives.confidence: High. The owner stated the need and answered the open questions.
pattern_narratives.current_state: The output shows words, characters and lines. It shows no longest-line figure.

pattern_narratives.applies_to: The longest-line measure and the existing `lines` field.
pattern_narratives.frequency: Every input that does not end with a line terminator.
pattern_narratives.severity: Medium. Readers may take the two fields as inconsistent.
pattern_narratives.confidence: High. The owner decided that the final segment counts for the longest-line measure.
pattern_narratives.current_state: The `lines` field excludes the unterminated final segment. The longest-line measure will include it.

pattern_narratives.applies_to: The word rule, the line terminator set and the runtime dependencies.
pattern_narratives.severity: Medium. A second definition of word or line would make fields disagree.
pattern_narratives.confidence: High. The owner requires reuse of SPEC-0001 to SPEC-0005 and no new runtime dependency.
pattern_narratives.current_state: The word rule and the line terminator set exist in the approved specs. The runtime dependency list is empty.

pattern_narratives.applies_to: The output line, the README and the existing tests.
pattern_narratives.frequency: Every run of wordcount, and every test of the output line.
pattern_narratives.severity: Medium. A wrong label, wrong position or changed field would break parsers and tests.
pattern_narratives.confidence: High. The owner fixed the label and the position.
pattern_narratives.current_state: The output line has three fields. The README and the tests assert that three-field line.

DISCOVER.Does the unterminated final segment coun: Include it — report 3. The unterminated final segment DOES count as a line for the longest-line measure, even though the existing `lines` counter excludes it. So `a b c` with no terminator reports longest_line_words: 3.
DISCOVER.Should the output report only the word c: Word count only. Report a single numeric field; no line number, no line text.
DISCOVER.What exact label should the new field us: Use the label `longest_line_words: N` and place it at the end, after `lines: <L>`. Output becomes `words: W characters: C lines: L longest_line_words: N`.
